reusePolicy: No established reuse license. These are independently summarized interface facts and audit findings, not copied implementations.

questions.establishedTask: Replace an inclusive bit interval in a 32-bit word with another word shifted into that interval.
clarityRequirements: Bit zero is the least significant position; both bounds are inclusive.
State that the inserted value fits the interval, rather than allowing its high bits to modify unrelated positions.
Define signed integer versus 32-bit pattern interpretation in all five languages.
Test j=31 and the full-width interval; shifting a 32-bit value by 32 must not silently wrap the count.
Do not present the source helper's zero-on-invalid-bounds behavior as an established book requirement.

questions.establishedTask: Render a number strictly between zero and one as a terminating binary fraction, reporting failure when it exceeds a fixed output bound.
questions.sourceDiscrepancy: The two public methods use different length guards: greater-than versus greater-than-or-equal-to 32. Their initial decimal-point character contributes to length. They therefore disagree at the boundary.
clarityRequirements: Choose and disclose one exact bank convention for the point, any leading zero, fractional-bit count and total character count.
Distinguish the actual binary64 argument from an exact decimal rational that its spelling might suggest.
Test exact powers of two on both sides of the chosen limit, 0.5, 0.125, 0.1, zero and one.
No rounding, ellipsis or tolerance may turn an overlong representation into a valid result.

questions.establishedTask: Find the longest consecutive-one run in a 32-bit representation when one position may be treated as one.
clarityRequirements: Specify the fixed 32-bit width, including negative inputs and leading zero bits.
Define the all-ones case explicitly rather than implying an impossible extra bit.
Cover all zero bits, all one bits, adjacent zeros, a zero separating long runs, and bit 31.
Explain why a sliding window with at most one zero is equivalent to the permitted flip, if that independent implementation is chosen.

questions.establishedTask: Find the nearest smaller and larger positive signed integers with the same number of set bits; absent neighbors have a sentinel.
clarityRequirements: State the positive 31-bit domain and order of the two returned neighbors.
Define absence independently on each side and include the signed maximum boundary.
Do not substitute the existing closest-integer-of-same-weight task, whose distance objective and tie behavior differ.
An independent reference can compare combinatorial bit patterns; avoid scanning billions of integers in boundary tests.

questions.establishedTask: Count differing positions between two 32-bit integer patterns.
clarityRequirements: Negative values use their 32-bit two's-complement patterns.
XOR identifies exactly differing positions; the explanation must match the chosen bit-count loop in each language.
Zero versus minus one differs in all 32 positions, not an unbounded signed representation.

questions.establishedTask: Swap every adjacent pair of bit positions in a 32-bit word.
clarityRequirements: Pairs are (0,1), (2,3), through (30,31), with bit zero least significant.
Specify logical right shifts and signed-result encoding.
Test the sign bit, alternating patterns, zero, all ones, and applying the operation twice.
Do not map this to swapping just two selected bit positions.

questions.establishedTask: Set an inclusive horizontal pixel interval in a byte-packed monochrome screen while preserving unrelated bits.
clarityRequirements: Width is in pixels and divisible by eight; explain row-major byte layout and high-bit-first pixels.
State whether byte observations use 0..255 or signed byte values; each language must display the same screen.
Preserve the original buffer and every bit outside the interval; drawing sets bits rather than clearing the row first.
Cover one pixel, both ends in one byte, full bytes, multi-byte partial edges, repeated drawing, nonzero initial screens, first/last rows.
